subject: 4.35 metre sailboat on an open directional sea
identity: The boat remains the clear subject at design distance.
Long swell, wind waves and capillary detail read as distinct wavelength bands.
Whitecaps are sparse, broken and attached to persistent compression regions.
Water reads as a dielectric interface over an absorbing body, not transparent blue plastic.
invariants: The CPU Gerstner sampler remains the sole owner of buoyancy and boat-water contact.
The spectral ocean uses a deterministic seed of 481516.
No ocean mesh edge is visible at the horizon.
No regular parallel comb or moire bands appear in chase or oblique cinematic views.
The final surface reads as irregular multi-scale patches rather than long uniform ribbons.
Sky reflection remains Fresnel-bounded and is broken up by the resolved spectral normal.
No shader program reports a runnable failure.
Camera transitions have one interpolation owner.
allowedDivergences: The project keeps a WebGL2 fragment-IFFT backend instead of requiring WebGPU and TSL.
Open-ocean transmission uses an analytic fallback depth because the app has no scene-depth or scene-colour prepass.
Foreground screen refraction is intentionally absent until a stable scene-colour ownership path exists.
Low and medium modes retain all three simulated cascades while material weights reduce fine detail.
